- Residency: Redwood can guarantee that production inference requests will be routed to APAC hosts only. We allow transient cross-region processing for DR and backups; our standard transient window is up to 72 hours but we can discuss shortening that for this account and specify it in the addendum. No routine processing will occur in EU/US for pinned workloads.

- Subprocessor activation: we will provide an activation checklist and target a window for APAC subprocessor activation after the addendum is fully executed. Tentative ops timeline is 15–21 business days post-signature to fully enable APAC pinning in our Dedicated/Private provisioning flow (longer if on-prem options are requested).

Jordan — draft language below we can offer as an addendum (legal ok to start with this); I attached a redlined PDF. Please review and confirm ops timeline in parallel.

--- Proposed DPA addendum paragraph ---
"Redwood Inference shall ensure that all inference requests for the CardioHealth production environment (as identified by tenant ID provided in Schedule A) are processed exclusively within the APAC (Singapore) region. Redwood may perform temporary cross-region processing strictly for disaster recovery, backup restoration, or incident response. Such transient processing shall not exceed 72 consecutive hours except where prior written consent is obtained from CardioHealth. Redwood shall provide notification within 24 hours if transient processing is initiated and shall include host locations and processing purpose. Redwood shall not export CardioHealth PII to jurisdictions outside APAC for routine processing. Any use of subprocessors for APAC processing shall be disclosed in Schedule B and activated following the activation timeline described in Appendix 1 to this addendum."

If CardioHealth wants a shorter transient window (e.g., 24–48h) we can propose that and mark it as negotiable. Also suggested: an emergency escrow option (customer-controlled key escrow) for short-term failovers — needs legal ops involvement and additional SOW.

FWIW from ops: the 15–21 business day target Jordan mentioned is realistic for our standard Dedicated provisioning if there are no infra blockers. Key ops checklist highlights below (I'll attach the full checklist):

- Pre-reqs: signed addendum + tenant ID + compliance questionnaire completed.
- Provisioning: reserve APAC GPU pool, deploy inference runtime variant with locale bindings, seed KV/cache in-region.
- Subprocessor activation: run onboarding scripts, enable network ACLs, rotate keys per KMS policy.
- DR window: we can set a controlled transient failover window (default safety max = 72 hours). We can tighten to 24/48 hours as Marissa suggests but that increases operational risk for longer failovers.
- Evidence: we will provide an ops runbook, a proof-of-deployment screenshot, and an activity log extract for the activation event.

Proposed timeline:
- Day 0: Signed addendum confirmed & PO received
- Day 1–3: Schedule infra reservation & initialize tenant config
- Day 4–10: Provision, smoke test in APAC, initial telemetry verification
- Day 11–15: Final validation, compliance evidence package assembled
- Day 16–21: Cutover and handover to customer, unless additional SOW items are requested

I've attached the detailed workbook: ops-activation-checklist.xlsx. I'll open INF-1227 and link the runbook; we should also create a DocuSign envelope once Legal confirms the final addendum (sample link: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123).
